newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress against Cardoso reelection - poll. [corrected 22:39 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress against Cardoso reelection - poll. [corrected 22:39 gmt]

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's chances of running for a second term in 1998 were dealt a blow on Sunday when a poll showed little support among congressmen.

Only 38 percent of deputies and 44 percent of senators backed the idea of rewriting the constitution to allow current holders of elected office to stand for reelection, according to the poll by newspapers O Globo and Estado de Sao Paulo.
Changes to the Brazilian constitution require two majorities of 60 percent in each house. A bill to allow reelection has been sent to Congress but has not yet begun committee-level discussions.

The poll, which canvassed 411 of Brazil's 513 deputies and 64 of 81 senators, found support of nearly 70 percent in both houses for the concept of reelection when not extended to current holders of office. (Corrects number of deputies canvassed)
Brazil's 1988 constitution ruled out reelection, partly in reaction to the authoritarian 1964-85 military dictatorship.

Cardoso has limited himself to backing the concept of reelection. But he is widely believed to want to emulate presidents Alberto Fujimori of Peru and Carlos Menem of Argentina by standing for a second term in the 1998 presidential elections.
